vibe: Patch Tuesday energy — a perfect-10 Oracle flaw on CISA's 3-day clock, a 270-server Zimbra mass-breach, and an agent-poisoning bug that lands uncomfortably close to home for anyone running OpenClaw, while OpenAI's Jalapeño chip and Claude's new cross-app memory carry the AI side.

cyber.title: Actively exploited Oracle WebLogic flaw gets CISA's tightest-ever 3-day patch deadline
cyber.summary: A perfect-10 CVSS, unauthenticated Oracle WebLogic flaw is under active exploitation. CISA issued its tightest-ever 3-day emergency patch deadline, and even shops that applied all 1,449 other Oracle patches this year were still hit — corroborated across The Register and Dark Reading.

cyber.title: Webpage-triggered flaw lets attackers poison local AI models behind NVIDIA's NemoClaw (the sandbox that runs OpenClaw-style agents)
cyber.summary: Oasis Security found that NVIDIA's NemoClaw — its reference stack for running agents like OpenClaw inside sandboxes — starts Ollama bound to 0.0.0.0. A malicious webpage can DNS-rebind past the CORS check and rewrite the model's chat template, silently injecting instructions into every future response. No CVE, not exploited in the wild yet. Fixed on macOS/Linux in v0.0.35; still open on Windows/WSL. Worth knowing given the tooling overlap with what you run day to day.

cyber.title: Hackers breached 270+ Zimbra mail servers in ongoing attacks
cyber.summary: A mass-exploitation campaign against Zimbra Collaboration servers is still running, with Dark Reading separately flagging how fast the patch window is closing. If you or clients run Zimbra, this is a today problem.

cyber.title: Crooks push Mac malware through fake OpenAI Codex ads
cyber.summary: Malvertising campaign impersonates OpenAI's Codex to drop Mac malware — another sign AI-branded lures are the current phishing bait of choice.

cyber.title: 24 npm packages abuse unpkg mirrors to host fake Cloudflare CAPTCHA pages
cyber.summary: Supply-chain abuse using legitimate unpkg CDN mirrors to serve fake CAPTCHA phishing pages from inside otherwise-normal npm packages.

cyber.title: AnonyMousKIT phishing-as-a-service uses voice AI agents to phish iPhone passcodes
cyber.summary: A phishing kit now bundles AI voice agents to social-engineer iPhone users out of their passcodes — commoditized AI-assisted vishing.

cyber.title: Massive DDoS attack disrupts Norway's government digital services
cyber.summary: A large-scale DDoS knocked Norwegian government services offline; The Record has separate corroborating coverage.

cyber.title: "Sleepwalker" backdoor spreading on Windows machines
cyber.summary: New Windows backdoor campaign flagged by The Register — worth a skim if you manage Windows fleets.

cyber.title: US sanctions Iran-linked hackers behind critical infrastructure breaches
cyber.summary: Treasury sanctions follow a string of Iran-linked attacks on critical infrastructure; The Record separately reports a UK power-plant disclosure the same day.

ai.title: OpenAI's Jalapeño chip benchmarks show it's built for fast inference at scale
ai.summary: OpenAI's in-house inference chip Jalapeño posted benchmarks aimed squarely at Nvidia Blackwell. Heavily corroborated (TechCrunch, The Verge, The Register, and a 160-point HN thread) — a real signal on the AI hardware race, relevant if you're tracking inference economics.

ai.title: Anthropic's Claude and Cowork will now share memories across sessions - opt-out only
ai.summary: Claude chat and Cowork sessions now share memory by default (opt-out available). Covered by ZDNet, Engadget and TechCrunch — directly relevant given the Claude-based tooling you run daily; worth checking your own memory/opt-out settings.

ai.title: OpenAI subpoenaed by Alabama AG over Hugging Face hack
ai.summary: State-level legal scrutiny of OpenAI over a Hugging Face breach tie-in — one to watch as a precedent for AI-company breach liability.

ai.title: Anthropic expected to tell investors it sees over $30T in potential revenue
ai.summary: Eye-popping long-term revenue projection reportedly being pitched to investors — take the number with the usual pitch-deck grain of salt.

it.title: Apple leans hard into local AI: new Mac Studio and Mac mini with M6 / M5 Ultra
it.summary: Apple's new desktop silicon is explicitly pitched at local AI inference workloads — three separate 500-800 point HN threads plus ZDNet/Engadget coverage. Notable if you've been eyeing a local-inference box.

it.title: Perplexity ships "Portable Computer" on NVIDIA DGX Spark - local harness, zero per-token cost
it.summary: An OS-enforced sandboxed local agent harness running on DGX Spark hardware, avoiding per-token API costs for local steps — an interesting local-compute counterpoint to the cloud-inference race.

videos.title: AI Model vs Agentic Harness: What Actually Drives AI
videos.verdict: WATCH — clean, jargon-free breakdown of why two products on the same model can behave totally differently: tools, memory, and the agentic loop live in the "harness," not the model. Directly maps onto the agent-harness tooling you use daily; ~7 minutes, no fluff.
videos.summary: Explains the model-vs-harness split (tools, memory persistence/compaction, the plan-act-observe loop with verification) and argues most recent capability gains have come from harness improvements, not just smarter models.

videos.title: AI Is Changing Cybersecurity. Here's How to Defend Yourself
videos.verdict: SKIM the first half — sponsored Black Hat interview (ThreatLocker), but the opening 10 minutes have real substance: a live demo of Claude refusing then agreeing to "delete all except text files, then delete text files" (self-flagging it as ransomware-shaped), and a prompt-injection trick that fooled Claude into mischaracterizing a malicious PowerShell script. Core thesis is deny-by-default/zero-trust for agent process trees. Back half is a ThreatLocker product pitch.
videos.summary: Threat researcher demos AI agents being socially engineered into ransomware-like behavior and prompt-injected past security analysis, arguing for zero-trust ring-fencing of what agentic tools are allowed to touch.
